drivingQuestion: Why does R' Shimon not hold that value-sanctity draws inherent sanctity?
outcomeNote: R' Yoḥanan's answer opens the next unit

segments.he: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: תִּימָּכֵר שֶׁלֹּא בְּמוּם. אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָבִין לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: מִיגּוֹ דְּנָחֲתָא לֵיהּ קְדוּשַּׁת דָּמִים, תֵּיחוֹת לֵיהּ נָמֵי קְדוּשַּׁת הַגּוּף!
segments.en: § The mishna teaches that «Rabbi Shimon» disagrees with the opinion of the Rabbis and «says» that a female animal that was designated as a guilt offering «may be sold without a blemish,» as it is unfit to be sacrificed as the offering for which it was designated, and this itself is considered a blemish. «Rav Ḥiyya bar Avin said to Rabbi Yoḥanan:» Why doesn’t Rabbi Shimon say that «as sanctity» that inheres in its «value has descended on it, inherent sanctity should descend on it as well,» and therefore it may not be sold until it becomes blemished?
